anomalies.observed: The Q2 gate node (R2 pull-up junction, Q2 gate pin) runs up to x≈884 and drops onto U5 pin 31 (P4_LED). The LED3 global label also lands on that same vertical stub at U5 pin 31, so the keyboard LED3 net appears to share U5.31 with the EPD display-power MOSFET gate.
anomalies.expected: The specification says U5.31 is a dedicated general-purpose output driving only the Q2 display-power gate. It does not mention any keyboard LED on that pin. The keyboard LED3 line (U4 LEDK_2_3) should be on its own GPIO, separate from the Q2 gate net.

evidence.quote: U5.31 (SKW92A GPIO, datasheet pin 31 = P4_LED/GPIO#39, repurposed here as a general output)
SkylabModule.kicad_sch, U5 bottom pins 30–31: wire from Q2 gate junction (793,497) runs to pin 31 (884,478), and the LED3 global label tip at (884,508) sits on the same pin-31 stub

anomalies.impact: If the connection is real, keyboard LED3 activity and the firmware's control of the display-power switch share one pin. This can glitch the EPD power rail or leave the LED and display-power gate fighting each other.

parsed.summary: Most of the power, regulator, battery, EPD boost and interface wiring matches the specification. The one suspicious finding is that the LED3 label appears to share U5 pin 31 with the Q2 display-power gate, which the specification does not describe. The reading is uncertain because the drawing is low-resolution at that junction.
